title: Critical regions and critical values
keyIdea: In a hypothesis test, the critical region is the set of values of the test statistic that lead you to reject H₀, and the critical value is its boundary, the first value inside it. For a binomial test, take the most extreme values in the direction of H₁ and make the region as large as possible while its probability under H₀ stays at or below α; for a two-tailed test each tail may hold at most α/2. For X ~ B(20, 0.3) at 5%, H₁: p > 0.3 gives X ≥ 10, because P(X ≥ 10) = 4.80% but P(X ≥ 9) = 11.33%. If the observed value lies in the region, reject H₀. The actual significance level is the probability of the region under H₀.
familyTip: Toss a coin 20 times together and count heads. Before you start, agree which counts would make you doubt the coin is fair, such as 15 or more heads or 5 or fewer. That list is a critical region; see whether your count lands in it.

visual.caption: H₀: p = 0.3. Where does the critical region go? Drag each card, or tap it and then a box.

items: Claim: the new seed germinates more often

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag the boundary of a binomial critical region, read critical values from a table, split α over two tails, decide tests.

kid: Before a test, you decide which results would make you reject H₀. That set of results is the critical region. The first value inside it is the critical value.
The region sits at the end that H₁ points to. If H₁ says p > 0.3, big counts are evidence, so the region is X ≥ c. If H₁ says p < 0.3, it is X ≤ c.
Make the region as big as you can while its chance under H₀ stays at or below α. For X ~ B(20, 0.3) at 5%, P(X ≥ 10) = 4.80% but P(X ≥ 9) = 11.33%. So the region is X ≥ 10.
For a two-tailed test, split α. At 5%, each tail may hold at most 2.5%. Then check your result. If it is in the region, even right on the critical value, reject H₀. If not, do not reject H₀.
adult: Ages 16 to 18. This is A level Mathematics statistics for England: conduct a statistical hypothesis test for the proportion in the binomial distribution, and know the terms critical value, critical region, acceptance region, significance level and actual significance level. One-tailed and two-tailed tests are both required.

The lab uses H₀: p = 0.3 with n = 20. To 4 decimal places P(X ≤ 1) = 0.0076, P(X ≤ 2) = 0.0355, P(X ≤ 3) = 0.1071, P(X ≤ 9) = 0.9520 and P(X ≤ 10) = 0.9829. So at 5% the upper region is X ≥ 10 (4.80%), the lower region is X ≤ 2 (3.55%), and the two-tailed region is X ≤ 1 or X ≥ 11, with actual level 0.764% + 1.714% ≈ 2.48%.

Common mistakes. Taking the table row as the upper critical value (9 instead of 10, since P(X ≥ 10) = 1 − P(X ≤ 9)). Choosing the tail probability closest to α even when it is above α. Putting the whole of α in each tail of a two-tailed test. Not rejecting H₀ when the observed value equals the critical value. Quoting α as the actual significance level, and saying H₁ is proved.

practice.prompt: X ~ B(20, 0.3) under H₀, H₁: p > 0.3, 5% level. Which is the critical region?
practice.explain: X ≥ 10 holds 4.80%, within 5%. Adding 9 would make it 11.33%, too much, and X ≥ 11 leaves out 10, which is allowed.

practice.prompt: For an upper-tail test, the first table row with P(X ≤ x) ≥ 0.95 is x = {r}. What is the critical value?
practice.hint: P(X ≥ c) = 1 − P(X ≤ c − 1). Which c uses row {r}?
practice.explain: 1 − P(X ≤ {r}) is P(X ≥ {=r+1}), so the region is X ≥ {=r+1} and the critical value is {=r+1}.

practice.prompt: A two-tailed test at the 10% level. How much probability may each tail hold?
practice.hint: The two tails share α between them.
practice.explain: Each tail gets half of α: at most 5% in each. X is discrete, so a tail is rarely exactly 5%.

practice.prompt: The critical region is X ≥ {c}. Under H₀, P(X ≤ {=c-1}) = 0.9{k}. What is the actual significance level, as a percentage?
practice.hint: The region X ≥ {c} is everything except X ≤ {=c-1}.
practice.explain: P(X ≥ {c}) = 1 − 0.9{k} = 0.0{=10-k}, so the actual significance level is {=10-k}%.

practice.prompt: The critical region is X ≤ 2. You observe X = 2. What do you conclude?
practice.hint: Is 2 inside X ≤ 2? The critical value belongs to the region.
practice.explain: 2 is the critical value and lies inside the region, so reject H₀.

pool.prompt: X ~ B(20, 0.3) under H₀, H₁: p < 0.3, 5%. P(X ≤ 2) = 0.0355, P(X ≤ 3) = 0.1071. Critical region?
pool.hint: Lower tail, and stay at or below 0.05.
pool.explain: P(X ≤ 2) = 0.0355 ≤ 0.05 and P(X ≤ 3) = 0.1071 is not, so the region is X ≤ 2.

choices: The first value inside the critical region
pool.hint: It marks a boundary on the X scale.
pool.explain: The critical value is the boundary value of X that is in the critical region, such as 10 in X ≥ 10.

pool.prompt: A student picks X ≥ 9 because P(X ≥ 9) = 5.4% is closer to 5% than P(X ≥ 10) = 2.1%. What is wrong?
choices: The region must not hold more than α
pool.explain: The probability of the region must be at or below α. 5.4% is too much, so the region is X ≥ 10.

pool.hint: Each tail may hold at most 2.5%.
pool.explain: 0.76% and 1.71% are both within 2.5%; 3.55% and 4.80% are not. So X ≤ 1 or X ≥ 11.

pool.prompt: The critical region is X ≥ 10 and you observe X = 8. What do you conclude?
choices: Do not reject H₀: not enough evidence that p > 0.3
pool.hint: Is 8 in the region? And does a test ever prove H₀?
pool.explain: 8 is outside X ≥ 10, so do not reject H₀. That is not proof that H₀ is true.

pool.prompt: The region X ≤ 1 or X ≥ 11 has tails 0.764% and 1.714%. What is the actual significance level?
pool.hint: Add the probabilities of both tails.
pool.explain: 0.764% + 1.714% ≈ 2.48%. That is the chance of rejecting H₀ when it is true.

pool.prompt: Why is the actual significance level usually less than α in a binomial test?
choices: X takes whole numbers, so tail sums jump
pool.hint: Can you add half a bar to a tail?
pool.explain: X is discrete, so the tail grows in jumps (4.80% to 11.33%). The largest region within α usually holds less than α.

pool.prompt: For a lower-tail test, the last table row with P(X ≤ x) ≤ α is x = {r}. What is the critical value?
pool.hint: For a lower tail, P(X ≤ c) is read straight from the table.
pool.explain: The region is X ≤ {r}, so the critical value is {r} itself.

pool.prompt: An upper-tail critical region is X ≥ {c} for n = 20. How many values of X are in the critical region?
pool.hint: X can be any whole number from 0 to 20.

pool.prompt: P(X ≤ 9) = 0.9520 under H₀. A student says the critical value is 9. What is the slip?
pool.explain: 1 − P(X ≤ 9) is the probability of 10 or more, so the region is X ≥ 10 and the critical value is 10.
